correctness.rationale: Higashitani–Padrol–Sanyal coordinate product decomposition applies to every full-dimensional sampled 0/1 polytope. Every coordinate-prism event has exact probability b^(2^(n-1)); pairwise intersections have (p^4+q^4)^(2^(n-2)) and exponentially smaller rate. For every non-singleton split, the independent column probability is bounded by rho_p^2^n for rho_p<sqrt(b), uniformly over split sizes; at most exp(o(2^n)) split choices. The cube-hyperplane enumeration gives exponentially negligible affine-deficiency probabilities both unconditionally and inside a prism event. Exclusion of double-prism and other product splits yields a unique segment factor plus an indecomposable complement. The exact inclusion-exclusion identity follows from subcube-constant indicators. A standard-library checker tests inequalities and exhaustively enumerates 3- and 4-cube subsets; it is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Determines an exponentially rare but naturally defined geometric event in the standard random Boolean polytope model with its exact dimension-dependent leading prefactor. Further identifies the overwhelmingly dominant exceptional polytope geometry and a sharp separation between singleton prism and all higher-dimensional factors. This is not implied by routine high-probability indecomposability and gives a structural probability law with relevant finite-n checkable formula.
